He is also a published poet, freelance writer, activist, and motivational speaker, as well as a co-host of ''Centers of Attention'', a sports talk show on ESPN Radio Syracuse in [[Syracuse, New York|Syracuse]], New York, alongside former professional basketball player [[Danny Schayes]]. ==Early life== His name is derived from the [[Eighteenth dynasty of Egypt|18th dynasty]] "heretic pharaoh" [[Akhenaten]], an ancient Egyptian king.Steinberg, Dan (October 27, 2006). [https://web.archive.org/web/20130220073134/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/dcsportsbog/2006/10/a_dcu_name_mystery_is_solved_a.html "A DCU Name Mystery is Solved, and a Wizards Name Mystery Emerges"]. ''[[The Washington Post]]''. ==Career== ===College=== Thomas played his [[college basketball]] at [[Syracuse University]] from 1996 to 2000, where he averaged 11 points per game and almost seven rebounds per game and graduated with a degree in business management.{{cite news |last1=Pitoniak |first1=Scott |title=SU's Thomas just a flick of his wrist from blocks mark |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/67874292/ |access-date=17 January 2021 |work=[[Democrat and Chronicle]] |date=29 November 1999 |archive-url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/67874160/ |archive-date=17 January 2021 |pages=22, 28 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] {{open access}}}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/commentary/story/_/id/7804204/david-stern-mark-cuban-wrong-nba-age-limit |title=End the NBA draft age limit |work=ESPN.com |date=April 12, 2012 |access-date=August 9, 2013}} In his sophomore season, he was named the [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Most Improved Player|Big East Most Improved Player]]; in his junior and senior years he was named [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of the Year|Big East Defensive Player of the Year]]. At the end of his Syracuse career, Thomas was drafted 12th overall in the [[2000 NBA draft]] by the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. He also played basketball at Booker T. Washington High School in Tulsa, OK, where he was a teammate of [[De'mond Parker]], [[R. W. McQuarters]] and [[Ryan Humphrey]]. ===Professional career=== Without ever playing a game for the Mavericks, he was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2001.Rob Woodfork, [https://wtop.com/washington-wizards/2017/05/etan-thomas-still-doing-dirty-work-in-washington/ Etan Thomas still doing dirty work in Washington], wtop.com, USA, May 29, 2017 He would play for Washington for the next 8 years (technically 7, as he sat out the entire 2007–2008 season due to injury), with his best season being in 2003–2004 when he averaged 8.9 points and 6.7 rebounds. Although Thomas never averaged 1.0 assists in a season, that 03–04 season was the closest he came to it, recording 68 assists in 79 games, for a season average of 0.9. During the Wizards' training camp for the [[2007–08 NBA season]], a routine physical examination discovered that he had a leaking [[aortic valve]]. On October 11, 2007, Thomas successfully underwent open heart surgery. He returned to play for the Wizards on October 29, 2008, a full year after his surgery. In his first game back, he had 10 points and eight rebounds.{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/writers/marty_burns/11/06/thomas.wizards/index.html |title=Wizards' Thomas back – as starter, no less – after heart surgery |work=SI.com |date=November 6, 2008 |access-date=August 9, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023225602/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/writers/marty_burns/11/06/thomas.wizards/index.html |archive-date=October 23, 2012 }} On June 23, 2009, he was traded along with [[Oleksiy Pecherov]], [[Darius Songaila]], and a first-round draft pick to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for [[Randy Foye]] and [[Mike Miller (basketball, born 1980)|Mike Miller]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4282279 |title=Source: Foye, Miller head to Wiz |work=ESPN.com |date=June 24, 2009 |access-date=August 9, 2013}} A month later on July 27, 2009, he was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] along with a 2010 second-round draft pick and a conditional 2010 second-round draft pick in exchange for guards [[Chucky Atkins]] and [[Damien Wilkins]].{{cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=4630 |title=Timberwolves trade Etan Thomas, picks to Thunder for Damien Wilkins, Chucky Atkins |work=InsideHoops.com |date=July 27, 2009 |access-date=August 9, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303233521/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=4630 |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |url-status=dead }} On September 2, 2010, it was announced that the [[Atlanta Hawks]] had signed Thomas.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/Etan_Thomas_090210.html |title=Hawks Sign Etan Thomas |work=NBA.com |date=September 2, 2010 |access-date=August 9, 2013}} His tenure with the Hawks (2010–2011) would be his final season in the NBA. That season, he played 13 games for Atlanta while averaging 2.5 points and 1.8 rebounds. His final NBA game was played on April 16, 2011, in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference First Round against the Orlando Magic. Thomas played for 6 and half minutes and the only stat he recorded was 1 rebound in a 103–93 victory over Orlando. He would sit out for the remainder of the playoffs and the Atlanta Hawks were eventually eliminated in the Semi-Finals in 6 games by the Chicago Bulls. ==Other work== In 2005, Thomas released a book of poetry titled ''More Than an Athlete: Poems by Etan Thomas'' which included works critical of former Wizards head coach [[Doug Collins (basketball)|Doug Collins]].Boren, Cindy (May 22, 2016). [https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/early-lead/wp/2016/05/22/ex-nba-center-shames-woman-he-says-wouldnt-let-him-sit-by-her-on-train-due-to-race/ "Ex-NBA center shames woman he says wouldn’t let him sit by her due to race"]. ''The Washington Post''. In 2012, Thomas co-authored the autobiography ''Fatherhood: Rising to the Ultimate Challenge'', which he discusses his fatherless childhood and the importance of fatherhood.[https://books.google.com/books?id=mCoY1CXgKEIC Fatherhood: Rising to the Ultimate Challenge – Google]{{cite web|last=Lindgren|first=Michael|title="Fatherhood: Rising to the Ultimate Challenge" by Etan Thomas with Nick Chiles|url=https://articles.washingtonpost.com/2012-07-27/news/35487414_1_black-men-fatherhood-single-mother|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130628030731/http://articles.washingtonpost.com/2012-07-27/news/35487414_1_black-men-fatherhood-single-mother|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 28, 2013|work=washingtonpost.com|date=July 27, 2012|access-date=August 9, 2013}} Since 2020, Thomas has been a writer and podcaster for Basketballnews.com.[https://www.basketballnews.com/news/authors/etan-thomas Etan Thomas Basketball News] In 2022 he published: Police Brutality and White Supremacy: The Fight Against American Traditions. == Personal life == A [[Baptist]], Thomas is a member of the [[First Baptist Church of Glenarden]] and is involved in facilitating youth forums.Brian Lamb, [https://www.c-span.org/video/?442884-1/qa-etan-thomas Q&A Etan Thomas], c-span.org, USA, March 23, 2018 ==Political activism and social causes== [[File:Etan Thomas at the September 15, 2007 anti-war protest 2.jpg|thumb|Thomas at an anti-war protest in 2007]] Thomas says that he became an oralist when, after he was detained and humiliated by police officers in high school, his speech teacher had him sort and verbalize his feelings into a speech. The Tulsa World Newspaper published a story on his experience.{{Cite web|url=https://www.c-span.org/video/?442884-1/qa-etan-thomas|title=Q&A with Etan Thomas|website=C-SPAN.org|language=en-US|access-date=2018-10-29}} His mother spoke with him about activists who used their positions as athletes to amplify their reach, such as [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]], [[Muhammad Ali]], [[Bill Russell]], and [[Jim Brown]]. In his book, ''More Than an Athlete'', Thomas discusses how the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA)]] runs as a business, and not to the service of the student athletes. After his wife was injured in college, the NCAA fought to take away her scholarship, and therefore, her ability to pay for and attend college. He points out the hypocrisy in an organization who makes billions a year and claims that there is not enough funding available for their main sources of profit, the athletes. In September 2005, Thomas was one of several celebrities to speak at an anti-war rally in [[Washington, D.C.]]{{cite web|last=Zirin|first=Dave|title=The Speech Everyone Is Talking About: Etan Thomas|url=http://www.commondreams.org/views05/0927-20.htm|work=Commondreams.org|date=September 27, 2005|access-date=August 9, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120630103255/http://www.commondreams.org/views05/0927-20.htm|archive-date=June 30, 2012}} He also spoke out at the [[September 15, 2007 anti-war protest]] in Washington, D.C.{{cite news|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/etan-thomas/in-defense-of-barack-obam_b_70922.html |title=In Defense of Barack Obama |work=Huffingtonpost.com |date=November 2, 2007 |access-date=August 9, 2013}} He blogs for ''[[The Huffington Post]]''.Hutchins, Brett; Rowe, David (April 27, 2012). [https://books.google.com/books?id=UDjo4verYYcC&q=EtanThomas%2Cblogger%2Chuffington&pg=PA77 ''Sport Beyond Television: The Internet, Digital Media and the Rise of Networked Media Sport'']. Routledge Research in Cultural and Media Studies, p. 77. Archived at [[Google Books]].[http://www.huffingtonpost.com/etan-thomas/ "Etan Thomas"]. ''[[The Huffington Post]]''. Thomas said he was inclined to be against the Iraq War, as he felt there was no clear reason to invade the country and the fact that some of his brother's friends who were deployed to Iraq, and upon learning about how terrified they were, decided to begin speaking out. Thomas actively supported [[Barack Obama]]'s 2008 campaign for [[President of the United States|U.S. president]]. On August 16, 2008, he appeared with [[Democratic National Committee]] chair [[Howard Dean]] at stops in northern Virginia as part of the Democratic National Committee's "Register for Change" bus tour to encourage local voter registration drives. Thomas gave speeches at two stops in [[Fairfax County, Virginia|Fairfax County]][http://www.leedems.org/2008/08/16/howard-deans-register-for-change-bus-tour/ Howard Dean’s Register for Change Bus Tour] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120310143559/http://www.leedems.org/2008/08/16/howard-deans-register-for-change-bus-tour/ |date=2012-03-10 }} and the City of Alexandria. In January 2010, Thomas donated $30,000 to the Haiti relief efforts after the [[2010 Haiti earthquake]].{{cite web|url=http://newsok.com/thunder-notebook-russell-westbrook-donates-1000-per-point-to-haiti-relief/article/3434139 |title=Thunder notebook: Russell Westbrook donates $1,000 per point to Haiti relief
